name: Critical Care
description: Critical care , also known as intensive care , is specialized medical care provided to patients with life-threatening conditions that require constant monitoring and support from a multidisciplinary team of healthcare professionals. This care is typically administered in an Intensive Care Unit (ICU) . Patients in critical care may suffer from conditions such as severe infections, organ failure, respiratory distress, cardiac arrest, or major trauma. They often require advanced interventions like mechanical ventilation , intravenous medications , dialysis , or life support systems . Key features of critical care include: 24/7 monitoring by trained ICU staff Advanced life-saving equipment and technology Multispecialty collaboration for comprehensive treatment Strict infection control and patient safety protocols Personalized care plans to support recovery and stabilization Critical care plays a vital role in improving outcomes and survival rates for patients facing complex and rapidly changing medical conditions.
descriptionHtml:
Critical care, also known as intensive care, is specialized medical care provided to patients with life-threatening conditions that require constant monitoring and support from a multidisciplinary team of healthcare professionals. This care is typically administered in an Intensive Care Unit (ICU).

Patients in critical care may suffer from conditions such as severe infections, organ failure, respiratory distress, cardiac arrest, or major trauma. They often require advanced interventions like mechanical ventilation, intravenous medications, dialysis, or life support systems.

Key features of critical care include:

  • 24/7 monitoring by trained ICU staff
  • Advanced life-saving equipment and technology
  • Multispecialty collaboration for comprehensive treatment
  • Strict infection control and patient safety protocols
  • Personalized care plans to support recovery and stabilization

Critical care plays a vital role in improving outcomes and survival rates for patients facing complex and rapidly changing medical conditions.
